text:
anna: Quick sync — we need a concise PRD acceptance criteria for audit-evidence, KMS/HSM, and retention tiers before next week's roadmap review. Customers asking for 7y retention; SOC2/ISO asks ambiguous. Can we list tradeoffs and scope for launch? @mike @jamie @sarah

mike: Ok — quick brain dump of options and tradeoffs: 1) Default short retention (90d) keeps costs low and fits most customers. 2) Extended retention (7y) for enterprise: significant storage + egress costs, and HSM-backed key custody required for stronger non-repudiation. 3) Tiered storage: hot (30/90d) + cold (archive) — cheaper but slower exports. Key point: key rotation + deletion will affect ability to decrypt old logs unless we retain envelope keys or export keys with evidence bundles.

jamie: Implementation notes: we can implement per-tenant retention_policy + async archive job. Need to decide: a) do we re-encrypt archive with per-tenant archive key? b) do we keep a KMS-wrapped envelope key for each archive chunk? Also: export API must include key-id and signature so customers/auditors can verify integrity. Edge case: tenant requests immediate key rotation or key-delete — what do we do with past logs? We need a documented flow and UI warning.

sarah: From legal/compliance: SOC2 doesn't mandate specific retention length but requires demonstrable controls and ability to produce evidence. ISO/financial regs may demand multi-year retention. We must support: - proving chain of custody (who requested export/rotation) - redaction controls (PII) before export - SLA for evidence requests (e.g., 30 days to produce a signed bundle).

mike: Acceptance criteria proposal for PRD (short): 1) Product can produce a signed, timestamped evidence bundle for any 90-day window within retained range. 2) For enterprise customers, option to enable long-term archival (configurable up to 7 years) with HSM-backed key storage. 3) Key rotation docs: rotation does not make previously generated evidence unverifiable (we retain signatures/keys needed for verification or include key proof in exported bundle). 4) Access controls and audit trail present for all retention and export operations.

jamie: Example retention_policy schema we could use:```json
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "hot_ttl_days": 90,
  "archive": { "enabled": true, "ttl_days": 2555, "storage_class": "cold" },
  "kms_key_id": "projects/../keys/k-abc",
  "exportable": true
}
```Edge cases: partial retention for LLM request logs where only prompts must be retained but embeddings are PII-free. Need mapping rules.

deploy-bot: RFC created: https://internal.redwood/in/rfcs/PRD-crypto-evidence-1837654321 (draft). Canary job queued for test archive pipeline.

anna: Nice, thanks. Let's scope launch MVP: default retention 90d, tenant opt-in enterprise archive up to 7y (paid), exportable signed bundles, docs on key rotation/retention implications. Owners: mike -> security design + PRD acceptance text; jamie -> prototype archive + export API; sarah -> compliance language and SLAs. I'll draft the RFC today and request review from infra and legal. Please add short bullets to the RFC with any additional edge cases you foresee. :+1:
